Mount Kilimanjaro in northern Tanzania, at 5,895 metres the highest mountain in Africa, was first climbed to the summit on 6 October 1889. The German geographer Hans Meyer and the Austrian climber Ludwig Purtscheller reached it with the local guide Yohani Lauwo.

The snowy peak near the equator had been reported to Europe by the missionary Johannes Rebmann in 1848, and scholars at first refused to believe in snow so close to the equator. The Chagga people had long farmed its fertile lower slopes.

The mountain became a symbol of Tanzania, and tens of thousands now climb it each year. Its shrinking glaciers are a much-watched sign of climate change. It rises near the Serengeti and the great parks of the north.
